title: "The Little Theatre That Could" brings 115 years of Laredo stage history to the screen
excerpt: A new documentary by local filmmaker Danny Davila traces more than a century of Laredo Little Theatre, and it premieres Nov. 18 for one night only at Alamo Drafthouse Laredo.
content:
A new documentary is bringing more than a century of Laredo Little Theatre history to the screen, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

"The Little Theatre That Could," directed by local filmmaker Danny Davila of D Man Studios, traces the theater's history of bringing the arts to Laredo through live stage performances, using numerous playbills from its history and its comedy show "Comedy Jam for George," which has run for more than two decades, the Morning Times reported. The film also shows the behind-the-scenes work of maintaining the theater and keeping it operating.

The documentary premieres Nov. 18, for one night only, at Alamo Drafthouse Laredo, 11210 EastPoint Drive. The trailer was shown and the film announced Wednesday evening during the theater's 115th Gala at IBC's Annex Ballroom, according to the Morning Times.

Executive Director A.B. Barrera said, "We need people to keep coming to the theater."

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, November 9, 2026.
